title: Call tracer
hints: In `defer t.Enter("x")()`, `t.Enter("x")` is evaluated **immediately** (like any deferred call's arguments/function value); only the returned func is deferred. So `Enter` prints the enter line right away and returns a closure for the exit line.

The method needs a pointer receiver so `t.depth++` sticks. Build the indent with `strings.Repeat("| ", t.depth)` and print with `fmt.Fprintf(t.W, "%s> %s\n", indent, name)`. The returned closure captures `t` and `name`.

`if t.W == nil { return func() {} }`. Otherwise print, `t.depth++`, and `return func() { t.depth--; fmt.Fprintf(t.W, "%s< %s\n", strings.Repeat("| ", t.depth), name) }`. Since the closure runs from `defer`, it also runs during a panic — don't call `recover` in it.
